layers.title: Subsurface water and chlorine (DAN)
layers.what_it_is: How much hydrogen (counted as water) and chlorine Curiosity's neutron instrument sensed in roughly the top metre of ground under the rover, point by point along the track.
layers.units: weight percent water-equivalent hydrogen; weight percent absorption-equivalent chlorine
layers.source: Zenodo record 6974535, file DAN_Pixelization_Table_sol_3333.csv (DAN instrument team)
layers.credit_or_licence: cc-by-4.0; Sergei Nikiforov, Maya Djachkova, Denis Lisov (2022). Water and chlorine in the Martian subsurface along the traverse of NASA's Curiosity rover: DAN measurement profiles along the traverse [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6974535
layers.coverage_note: Landing to sol 3333 only (the table has no sol column; the limit is from the record's readme). The last pixel is at latitude -4.74984, 27155 m along a 38799 m track, so everything after that has no DAN value here. Chlorine exists only where the rover made an active (neutron-pulse) measurement.
layers.join_note: Points carry their own latitude and longitude; chain_m comes from snapping to the nearest route vertex (median 1.9 m, largest 30.9 m), then averaging into 5 m bins.

layers.title: Rock and soil chemistry (APXS)
layers.what_it_is: The chemical make-up of rocks and soil that Curiosity touched with its arm-mounted X-ray spectrometer, listed for each rover stop.
layers.units: weight percent of each oxide or element
layers.source: NASA PDS Geosciences Node, MSL APXS calibrated oxide-abundance products (RDR, '*rwp*' tables)
layers.credit_or_licence: NASA Planetary Data System, public domain. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Guelph (APXS team)
layers.coverage_note: Sols 46 to 4842 (archive lists sols 46 to 4842). All listed oxide tables were read. 1 measurement(s) made at a site/drive that is not a stop in site.json are left out.
layers.join_note: Each product name carries the sol, site and drive of the rover when the measurement was made (ap?_<clock>rwp<sol 4><site 3><drive 4>). site_drive is the stop id in data/site.json, so the join is exact; the spot itself is within arm's reach (about 2 m) of that rover position. The target name is joined through the unit letter and spacecraft clock of the raw file listed in extras/msl_apxs_activities_sol*.csv.

layers.title: Laser targets (ChemCam)
layers.what_it_is: The names and kinds of rocks and soils Curiosity zapped with its laser from each rover stop.
layers.source: NASA PDS Geosciences Node, MSL ChemCam LIBS archive, master observation list msl_ccam_obs.csv
layers.credit_or_licence: NASA Planetary Data System, public domain. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/LANL/CNES/IRAP (ChemCam team)
layers.coverage_note: Sols 19 to 4843. 77 laser rows (14 stop/target pairs) were taken at a site/drive that is not a stop in site.json and are left out.
layers.join_note: Joined by the list's own 'RMC Site' and 'RMC Drive' columns, which are the rover position counters that make up the stop id in data/site.json, so the join is exact and does not rely on the sol. The list's own distance column puts these laser targets 1.8 to 9.2 m from the mast (median 2.7 m), so each is placed at its stop.

layers.title: Solar storms predicted to reach Mars (DONKI)
layers.what_it_is: Recent NASA model runs that predict a solar eruption arriving at Mars, with the predicted arrival time.
layers.source: NASA CCMC DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information), WSA-Enlil simulations
layers.credit_or_licence: NASA open data (api.nasa.gov). Credit: NASA Community Coordinated Modeling Center
layers.coverage_note: Simulations dated 2026-09-15 to 2026-11-14 (60 days). A frozen snapshot, not a live feed.
layers.join_note: Not tied to a place: applies to Mars as a whole.
